problem_after:
![](images/b6/b698fe735caaf3bc260c1e921bb95596df8869eba67ec9ce72484b4d86cc8c69.png)

The graph of the function $z=f(x,y)$ is shown above. Which of the points shown are local minimum points?

Select all that apply.
solution_before:
A function $f(x,y)$ has a local minimum point at $(a,b)$ if $f(x,y)\ge f(a,b)$ for all points $(x,y)$ in a neighborhood of $(a,b).$ 

In other words, we can take a neighborhood of $(x,y)$-values such that the point $(x,y,f(x,y))$ is the lowest point on the graph in the neighborhood.

Such regions exist for the points $A$ and $D.$ Hence $A$ and $D$ are local minimum points.

**Note**: For the point $D({x}_{D},{y}_{D},{z}_{D}),$ there are points $(x,y)$ in the surrounding regions such that $f({x}_{D},{y}_{D})=f(x,y).$ However, since the definition of local extrema is non-strict, $f(x,y)\ge f(a,b)$, the point $D$ does satisfy the conditions for a local minimum.

![](images/0a/0a371aa559222bd28c37677bace18eb912bdc978e364bab4cb3d83f7a310de3f.png)

:topic/_knowledge-points.:topic/title: Global vs. Local Extrema and Critical Points of Multivariable Functions

question_before.:question/problem:
![](images/81/81604581fae8b25776727eca4450caa7d48c42a781706455ed585d5cfc4a25fa.png)

The graph of the function $z=f(x,y)$ is shown above. Which of the points shown are local maximum points?

Select all that apply.
question_before.:question/worked-solution:
A function $f(x,y)$ has a local maximum point at $(a,b)$ if $f(x,y)\le f(a,b)$ for all points $(x,y)$ in a neighborhood of $(a,b).$ 

In other words, we can take a neighborhood of $(x,y)$-values such that the point $(x,y,f(x,y))$ is the highest point on the graph in the neighborhood.

Such regions exist for the points $A$ and $C.$ Hence $A$ and $C$ are local maximum points.

**Note**: For the point $A({x}_{A},{y}_{A},{z}_{A}),$ there are points $(x,y)$ in the surrounding regions such that $f({x}_{A},{y}_{A})=f(x,y).$ However, since the definition of local extrema is non-strict, $f(x,y)\le f(a,b)$, the point $A$ does satisfy the conditions for a local maximum.
